t: This is Our Lady of Victories Roman Catholic Primary School, with its covered play area and boundary wall, in Kensington and Chelsea. It was designed by Edward Robert Robson, an English architect who was famous for the progressive spirit of his London state-funded school buildings in the 1870s and early 1880s. That is the reason this school building matters. It belongs to a period when new public schools were being built across the capital, and Robson was one of the people shaping what they looked like.
